mainTopic: Eye blemishes of a בכור: הריס, cataracts, חלזון and נחש, תבלול, and the tests for permanent pale spots and tears
overview: The גמרא explains the eye blemishes in the משנה that let a בכור be slaughtered. It first defines הריס as the eyelid. It then works out when a דק (cataract) is a מום: a black דק counts when sunken, and a white דק counts when floating. Next it learns from an elder, רבי שמעון בן יוסי לקוניא, that the חלזון and the נחש are one permanent blemish. The same story adds that a scholar may teach his students so they can rule on his own בכור, provided he taught the rule before his case came up. The גמרא shows that the משנה's תבלול follows רבי יוסי, who holds there are no blemishes in the white of the eye. It then gives the sources for both רבי יוסי and רבי מאיר. A new משנה follows on permanent pale spots and constant tears. The גמרא matches it to רבי יהודה, explains the feeding test of moist and then dry fodder over three months, and begins to discuss how much fodder is fed. That discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What does the word הריס mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what the משנה's word הריס means.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the 'ris'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion of the משנה by asking what the unusual word הריס means. This sets up רב פפא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed a הריס that was pierced, damaged, or split as a blemish. Before anyone can apply that rule, we need to know which part of the eye הריס refers to.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion that follows the משנה
A part of the eye named in the משנה (defined in the next step)

phrases.english: Gemara: What is the 'ris'?
phrases.notes: Start of the גמרא. It defines a word from the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה's list of eye blemishes
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word הריס in the משנה

steps.title: רב פפא says it is the eyelid
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that הריס is the outer border of the eye, meaning the eyelid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is the outer line (border) of the eye.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question: הריס means the outer wall of the eye, which is the eyelid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase תורא ברא literally means an 'outer row' or 'outer wall.' So a split or pierced eyelid is the blemish the משנה had in mind.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the definition

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
The outer line (border) of the eye.
phrases.notes: This means the eyelid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הריס is the eyelid, the outer border of the eye

steps.title: A sunken cataract is a blemish, a floating one is not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the משנה's word דק and quotes a ברייתא: a sunken דק is a מום, but a floating דק is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A cataract, a תבלול.' The Rabbis taught: A sunken cataract is a blemish. A floating one is not a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה, דק and תבלול. It then brings a ברייתא about when a דק counts as a מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא adds a detail the משנה left out. A דק sunk into the eye is a מום, but one floating on the surface is not. This rule is about to be challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: A cataract or film over the eye
Another eye growth listed in the משנה

phrases.english: 'A cataract, a tevallul'
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A sunken cataract is a blemish,
a floating one is not a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next term in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sunken דק is a מום. A floating דק is not.

steps.title: Another ברייתא teaches the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the first ברייתא with a different ברייתא that rules the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught the opposite!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction. Another ברייתא says a sunken דק is not a מום and a floating one is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two sources give exactly opposite rulings about the same kind of blemish. The גמרא now needs a way to show that they are talking about different cases.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught (introduces a contradicting ברייתא)

phrases.english: But it was taught the opposite!
phrases.notes: That is, sunken is not a blemish and floating is a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא in step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא that a sunken דק is a מום and a floating one is not
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא gives the reverse ruling, so the two sources contradict each other

steps.title: First answer: black part of the eye versus white part
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that one ברייתא is about the black part of the eye and the other is about the white part.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one is about the black part of the eye, and that one is about the white part.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to settle the contradiction by saying the two ברייתות are talking about different parts of the eye.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this answer, the first ברייתא (sunken is a מום) is about the black part of the eye. The second (floating is a מום) is about the white part. This answer will be rejected in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The black part of the eye (iris and pupil)
The white part of the eye

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is about the black part,
that one is about the white part.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא בַּשָּׁחוֹר הָא בַּלָּבָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by location in the eye
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seem to discuss the same case
steps.terutzMaskana: One is about the black part of the eye and one is about the white part (a temporary answer)

steps.title: There are no blemishes in the white of the eye
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the answer, because a known rule says there are no blemishes in the white part of the eye.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there are no blemishes in the white part!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. There is an established rule that nothing in the white of the eye counts as a מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the second ברייתא were about the white part, it could not call a floating דק a מום, because the white part never produces a מום. So that ברייתא must also be about the black part, and the contradiction comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: There are no blemishes in the white part of the eye

phrases.english: But there are no blemishes in the white part!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that one ברייתא is about the white part of the eye
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A known rule says the white part never has a מום, so no ruling of מום could be about it

steps.title: Final answer: a white cataract versus a black cataract
steps.stepSummary: Both ברייתות are about the black part of the eye. The difference is the color of the דק itself: white or black.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: this one is about a white cataract, and that one is about a black cataract.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer. The difference is not where the cataract sits but what color the cataract itself is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A black דק is a מום when it is sunken (the first ברייתא). A white דק is a מום when it is floating (the second ברייתא). Both are in the black part of the eye, so the rule about the white part is not a problem.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 5. There, 'white' and 'black' meant parts of the eye. Here they describe the color of the cataract itself, and both cases are in the black part of the eye.

phrases.english: Rather:
this one is about a white cataract,
phrases.notes: This is the second ברייתא: floating is a blemish.

phrases.english: that one is about a black cataract.
phrases.notes: This is the first ברייתא: sunken is a blemish.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, הָא בְּדוּק לָבָן, הָא בְּדוּק שָׁחוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by the color of the cataract
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The split was by location in the eye (white part versus black part)
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are in the black part of the eye. A black דק is a מום when sunken, and a white דק is a מום when floating.

steps.title: Support from יאשיה דמן אושא, with a memory aid
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה reports from יאשיה דמן אושא exactly this split between a black and a white דק, and gives the mnemonic ברקא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבה בר בר חנה said: יאשיה from אושא told me: A black cataract, if sunken, is a blemish; if floating, it is not. A white cataract, if sunken, is not a blemish; if floating, it is a blemish. And your memory aid is 'ברקא.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its final answer with an explicit statement that teaches the same distinction between a black and a white cataract.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יאשיה's teaching matches step 7 exactly, so the answer is not a guess. The memory aid ברקא refers to an eye disease where white patches float on the eye and count as a מום. That helps you remember that a white דק is a מום when it floats.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who reports the teaching
יאשיה from the town of אושא
An eye disease with floating white patches

steps.whatToRemember: Black דק: sunken is a מום, floating is not. White דק: floating is a מום, sunken is not. Think of ברקא, where white floats.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the practical rule for checking a בכור for a cataract, and it settles the contradiction between the two ברייתות.

phrases.english: As Rabba bar bar Ḥana said:
Yoshiya from Usha told me:

phrases.aramaic: דַּק שָׁחוֹר מְשׁוּקָּע — הֲרֵי זֶה מוּם,
phrases.english: a black cataract, if sunken, is a blemish;
if floating, it is not a blemish.
A white cataract, if sunken, is not a blemish;
if floating, it is a blemish.
And your memory aid: 'barka.'
phrases.notes: ברקא is a disease with white patches floating on the eye, and it counts as a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the final answer of step 7
steps.raayaObject: The split between a black and a white דק
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבה בר בר חנה in the name of יאשיה דמן אושא

steps.title: Are the snail and the snake one blemish or two?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה and asks whether חלזון and נחש describe one blemish or two separate ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A snail, a snake, or a berry.' A question was asked: Is the snail the same as the snake, or perhaps it means a snail or a snake?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next blemish in the משנה and asks a question about how to read it. The next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One option is that נחש just explains what kind of חלזון shape is meant, so they are one blemish. The other option is that they are two different shapes, and each one is its own מום.

keyTerms.meaning: A snail-shaped growth over the pupil
A question was asked before them

phrases.english: 'A snail, a snake, or a berry.'
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
Is the snail the same as the snake,
or perhaps it means a snail or a snake?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next term in the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether חלזון and נחש are one blemish or two separate blemishes

steps.title: The elder teaches that the snail and the snake are one blemish
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה reports a story from רבי יוחנן בן אלעזר. An elder, רבי שמעון בן יוסי לקוניא, told him that the חלזון in the eye is a permanent blemish, and that this is the same as the נחש the חכמים spoke of.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבה בר בר חנה said that רבי יוחנן בן אלעזר told him: 'There was an elder in our neighborhood named רבי שמעון בן יוסי לקוניא. I never passed in front of him, but one time I did. He said to me: Sit, my son, sit. This snail is a permanent blemish, and one may slaughter the animal because of it. And this is the snake that the חכמים mentioned.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question from step 9 with a story. An elder taught that the חלזון and the נחש are one and the same blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 asked whether חלזון and נחש are two blemishes or one. The elder says 'this is the נחש the חכמים mentioned,' so they are one blemish with two names. He also says it is permanent, so the בכור may be slaughtered because of it.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear — introduces a source that answers the question
Snail — a snail-shaped growth in the eye
Snake — a blemish named in the משנה
Permanent blemish — allows a בכור to be slaughtered

steps.whyThisMatters: This settles the question from step 9: the משנה is listing one blemish under two descriptions, not two separate blemishes.

phrases.english: Come and hear,
as Rabba bar bar Chana said:

phrases.aramaic: סָח לִי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Elazar told me:
There was a certain elder in our neighborhood,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹסֵי לָקוֹנְיָא שְׁמוֹ,
phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon ben Yosei Lakonya was his name,
and in all my days I never passed before him.
Once I did pass before him,
and he said to me: Sit, my son, sit.
phrases.notes: He wanted to teach him something so the student could rule on the elder's own בכור.

phrases.english: This snail is a permanent blemish,
so one may slaughter the animal because of it,
and this is the snake that the Sages mentioned.
phrases.notes: This is the key line: the חלזון and the נחש are the same blemish.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 9
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether חלזון and נחש are one blemish or two
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They are one blemish: the חלזון is the נחש the חכמים mentioned, and it is permanent.

steps.title: A teacher may instruct students, who then rule for him
steps.stepSummary: The elder adds that a person may not judge blemishes on his own animal. However, he may teach the הלכה to his students, and they may then rule for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even though the חכמים said that a person may not examine blemishes for himself, he may still teach the הלכה to students, and the students may rule for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The elder explains why he taught the student. The student can now use that teaching to permit the elder's own בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that an owner cannot declare his own בכור blemished, since he has a personal interest. The elder's way around this: he teaches the general rule, and the students apply it and decide for him. The ruling comes from them, not from him.

keyTerms.meaning: A person may not examine blemishes for himself (on his own בכור)
Teaches or issues a halachic ruling

phrases.english: And even though they said:
a person may not examine blemishes for himself,
still, he may teach the halacha to the students,
and the students may rule for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ: אֵין אָדָם רוֹאֶה מוּמִין לְעַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the elder's words and adds a procedural rule about who may rule on the elder's בכור
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An owner may not judge his own בכור, but he may teach students, and they may rule for him.

steps.title: Challenge: a scholar's ruling that benefits himself is not accepted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the elder's method using רב הונא's rule. A scholar who states a ruling only after the case comes up is not believed. Here the elder taught the ruling exactly when his own animal needed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי אבא said in the name of רב הונא: Any scholar who issues a halachic ruling: if he said it before the case happened, we listen to him. If not, we do not listen to him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the elder's method. It seems he taught the rule only at the moment it helped him, and רב הונא says such a ruling is not accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's concern is personal interest. A ruling first stated when it helps the scholar himself looks self-serving. The elder taught the rule right when his own בכור had this blemish, so it seems his students should not have relied on it.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say — introduces a contradicting source
Before the incident (before the case came up)
We listen to him (his ruling is accepted)

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Abba say in the name of Rav Huna:
Any Torah scholar
who comes to issue a halachic ruling (for his own case),
if he said it before the incident,
we listen to him,
and if not, we do not listen to him!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the method described in step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: The elder teaching his students so they could permit his own בכור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב הונא rejects a scholar's ruling stated only once his own case arises. The elder seems to have taught the rule at exactly that moment.

steps.title: Answer: the elder had been teaching this rule all along
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the elder had already been teaching this הלכה from the start, before his own case came up. So his ruling is accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: He too had been teaching this ruling from the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The elder did not invent the rule for his own animal; he had been teaching it beforehand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's rule only rejects a ruling first stated after the case arises. The elder had taught this ruling earlier, so he fits the 'before the incident' category. His students could rely on it.
steps.whatToRemember: The חלזון is the same blemish as the נחש, and it is permanent. A scholar's ruling that affects his own case is accepted only if he was already teaching it before the case arose.

phrases.english: He too
had been issuing this ruling from the beginning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיהוּ נָמֵי מוֹרֶה וּבָא הֲוָה מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual clarification placing the case inside the permitted category of רב הונא's rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The elder first taught the rule only when his own בכור needed it
steps.terutzMaskana: He had taught the rule before, so it counts as stated 'before the incident' and is accepted

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: what is a תבלול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה, which define the eye blemish called תבלול as a white thread that cuts across the ring of the iris.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a תבלול? A white line that cuts through the סירא (the ring of the iris).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next phrase of the משנה. This is a setup line for the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes the תבלול only as a white line crossing into the dark part of the eye. It says nothing about a black line crossing into the white. That detail sets up the question of whose opinion the משנה follows.

keyTerms.meaning: An eye blemish listed in the משנה
The ring around the iris, between the black and the white

phrases.english: What is a tevallul?
A white line that cuts through the ring of the iris.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיזֶהוּ תְּבַלּוּל? לָבָן הַפּוֹסֵק אֶת הַסִּירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תבלול is a white line crossing the ring of the iris into the dark part.

steps.title: Whose opinion is this משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא the משנה's definition of תבלול follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who wrote this part of the משנה. It is setting up a comparison with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the משנה mentions only a white line entering the black, the גמרא wants to know which view it follows. The answer will tie it to a known dispute.

phrases.english: Whose opinion is our mishna?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the author of the clause quoted in step 14
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view the משנה's definition of תבלול follows

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי יוסי: no blemishes in the white of the eye
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows רבי יוסי. In a ברייתא, רבי מאיר holds that both a white line entering the black and a black line entering the white are blemishes. רבי יוסי counts only the white entering the black, because there are no blemishes in the white of the eye.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי יוסי, as a ברייתא teaches: A white line entering the black, or a black line entering the white, is a blemish. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יוסי says: A white line entering the black is a blemish. A black line entering the white is not a blemish, because there are no blemishes in the white.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי יוסי. It brings a ברייתא where רבי יוסי counts only a white line entering the black as a blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists only the white-into-black case, which matches רבי יוסי. רבי מאיר would also count black-into-white, so the משנה is not his view. רבי יוסי's reason, 'no blemishes in the white,' is the same rule the גמרא used in step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
There are no blemishes in the white of the eye

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse the color of the line with the part of the eye it enters. 'Black entering the white' means a dark line crossing into the white part of the eye. רבי יוסי rejects that case because the white part cannot hold a blemish.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's תבלול (a white line entering the black) follows רבי יוסי. He holds there are no blemishes in the white of the eye, so only a line that reaches the black counts.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Yosei,
as it is taught in a baraita:
A white line that enters the black,
or a black line that enters the white,
is a blemish;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.aramaic: לָבָן וְנִכְנָס בַּשָּׁחוֹר — הֲרֵי זֶה מוּם,
phrases.english: A white line that enters the black is a blemish,
a black line that enters the white is not a blemish,
because there are no blemishes in the white.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15 with a ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Author of the משנה's definition of תבלול
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי, who limits eye blemishes to the black part because there are no blemishes in the white
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה follows רבי יוסי
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא recording the dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי

steps.title: רב asks for the source of רבי יוסי's view
steps.stepSummary: רב asks what the reason is behind רבי יוסי's view that a תבלול counts as a blemish only when white enters the black.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: What is the reason of רבי יוסי?
steps.whatsHappening: רב asks why רבי יוסי says there are no blemishes in the white of the eye. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the last step we learned רבי יוסי's ruling: only white entering the black is a blemish. Now רב wants the source for that ruling. He looks for a reason that the white part of the eye does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? (asking for the source of a view)

phrases.english: Rav said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yosei?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the רבי יוסי view quoted in Step 16
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for רבי יוסי's view that the white of the eye is not a place for blemishes

steps.title: The verse calls the white part 'fat of the eye', not just 'eye'
steps.stepSummary: רב brings the פסוק 'יצא מחלב עינימו'. It shows that the white of the eye is called 'the fat of the eye' and not simply 'the eye'. The תורה lists תבלול 'in his eye', so it must be in the eye proper, meaning the black.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'Their eyes stand out from fatness.' The fat of the eye is what it is called. Plain 'their eyes' is not what it is called.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers that a פסוק in תהלים names the white part of the eye 'the fat of the eye'. So when the תורה says 'in his eye', it does not mean the white part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה lists תבלול as a blemish 'בעינו', meaning 'in his eye'. רב shows that the white is given a special name, 'fat of the eye', so plain 'eye' means only the dark part. That explains why רבי יוסי says there are no blemishes in the white.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Their eyes stand out from fatness' (תהלים ע״ג:ז)
The fat of the eye, meaning the white part

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the פסוק in תהלים is about blemishes. It only shows what the white of the eye is called. That name is then used to read the word 'בעינו' in the blemish list.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'Their eyes stand out from fatness,'
'fat of the eye' is what it is called,
phrases.notes: The white part has its own name.

phrases.english: plain 'their eyes' it is not called.
phrases.notes: So 'in his eye' in the blemish list means the dark part.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 17
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The white of the eye is called 'fat of the eye', not 'eye'. So 'בעינו' excludes the white, and a blemish there does not count.

steps.title: What is רבי מאיר's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי מאיר counts a black line entering the white as a blemish too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר, what is his reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks for רבי מאיר's reason. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר seems to go against the reading of the פסוק just given. So the גמרא needs to explain how he can count blemishes that reach into the white.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir, what is his reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רבי יוסי's source to רבי מאיר's source
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי מאיר counts both directions, including a black line entering the white

steps.title: תבלול means something that mixes up the eye
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר learns from the word תבלול itself. It means something that 'mixes' (מבלבל) the eye, so any mixing of white and black counts, in either direction.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does the word 'תבלול' mean? Something that mixes up the eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי מאיר learns from the meaning of the word תבלול. It means mixing, so it does not matter which color crosses into which.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי reads the word 'בעינו' narrowly. רבי מאיר instead focuses on the word 'תבלול', which comes from 'בלבול', meaning mixing. Any line that mixes the white and the black fits that word, whether white enters the black or black enters the white.

keyTerms.meaning: An eye blemish where colors cross into each other

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי: 'בעינו' means the dark part only, because the white is called 'fat of the eye'. רבי מאיר: 'תבלול' means mixing, so either direction counts. The משנה follows רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: What is the meaning of the word 'tevallul'?
Something that mixes up the eyes.
phrases.notes: White and black mixed, in either direction.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 19
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word תבלול means mixing, so any crossing of colors counts, in either direction.

steps.title: משנה: permanent pale spots last eighty days
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists two eye blemishes, חוורוור and constant tears, if they are permanent. Pale spots count as permanent if they last eighty days. רבי חנניא בן אנטיגנוס adds that the animal must be checked three times during those eighty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Pale spots and tears that are permanent are blemishes. Which pale spots are permanent? Any that lasted eighty days. רבי חנניא בן אנטיגנוס says: We check it three times within eighty days.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It names two eye blemishes and starts by explaining when pale spots count as permanent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a permanent blemish lets a בכור be slaughtered, so the משנה needs a test for 'permanent'. The first opinion uses time: eighty days. רבי חנניא בן אנטיגנוס adds that the spots must show up at three checks during that time.

keyTerms.meaning: Pale or white spots on the eye

steps.whyThisMatters: Permanent versus temporary is the key question for a בכור. Only a permanent blemish allows it to be slaughtered outside the מקדש.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
Pale spots and tears that are permanent.
Which are the permanent pale spots?
Any that lasted eighty days.
Rabbi Chananya ben Antigonus says:

phrases.aramaic: בּוֹדְקִין אוֹתוֹ שָׁלֹשׁ פְּעָמִים בְּתוֹךְ שְׁמוֹנִים יוֹם.
phrases.english: We check it three times within eighty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the תבלול discussion ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pale spots are a permanent blemish if they last eighty days. רבי חנניא בן אנטיגנוס requires three checks within that time.

steps.title: משנה: the feeding test for permanent tears
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains how we know tears are permanent. The animal is fed moist food and then dry food as a cure. If it is still not healed, the tears are a blemish. Other feeding orders do not prove anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are permanent tears: If the animal ate moist and dry food from a rain-watered field, or moist and dry food from an irrigated field, or ate the dry and afterwards the moist, it is not a blemish. It is a blemish only once it eats the moist and afterwards the dry.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a feeding test to check whether flowing tears are permanent. Only one feeding order counts as a full test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The food is used like medicine. If the right order (moist first, then dry) does not heal the tears, they are truly permanent. If the animal ate in other ways and was not healed, that proves nothing, because the cure was not tried properly.

keyTerms.meaning: Rain, meaning a field watered only by rain

steps.confusionAlert: 'אינו מום' here does not mean the tears are fine. It means we cannot yet call them permanent, because the proper cure was never tried.

phrases.english: And these are permanent tears:
If it ate moist and dry food from a rain-watered field,
or moist and dry food from an irrigated field,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אָכַל הַיָּבֵשׁ וְאַחַר כָּךְ הַלַּח —
phrases.english: or it ate the dry and afterwards the moist,
it is not a blemish,
phrases.notes: The cure was not done properly, so nothing is proven.

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיֹּאכַל הַלַּח וְאַחַר כָּךְ הַיָּבֵשׁ.
phrases.english: until it eats the moist and afterwards the dry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה, moving from pale spots to tears
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tears are a permanent blemish only if they are not healed after eating moist food and then dry food.

steps.title: Whose view does the משנה follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא the משנה follows, especially its rule of eighty days for pale spots.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Whose view is our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking which תנא wrote the משנה. This sets up the answer from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The eighty-day rule for pale spots is not agreed by everyone. So the גמרא wants to find which side of a dispute the משנה follows.

phrases.english: Gemara:
Our Mishnah, whose view is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the author of the משנה just quoted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds the משנה's eighty-day rule for pale spots

steps.title: It is רבי יהודה, who requires eighty days for pale spots
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows רבי יהודה. In a ברייתא, רבי מאיר says pale spots need forty days and tears need eighty. רבי יהודה says pale spots need eighty days, just like the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי יהודה, as it is taught in a ברייתא: Permanent pale spots take forty days, and permanent tears take eighty days. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: Pale spots take eighty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי יהודה. It proves this from a ברייתא where רבי יהודה says eighty days for pale spots.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר gives pale spots a shorter time, forty days. רבי יהודה says eighty days, which matches the משנה. So the משנה follows רבי יהודה and not רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
These are the words of רבי מאיר

steps.whatToRemember: Pale spots: רבי מאיר says forty days, and רבי יהודה says eighty days. The משנה follows רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Yehuda, as it is taught:
Permanent pale spots take forty days,
and permanent tears take eighty days,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: חֲוַרְוָור — שְׁמוֹנִים יוֹם.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda says: pale spots take eighty days.
phrases.notes: This matches the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 23 with a ברייתא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי יהודה, who requires eighty days for pale spots, against רבי מאיר's forty days.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's test for permanent tears
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues with רבי יהודה's view. Fodder from an irrigated field proves nothing, and dry food before moist food proves nothing. Only dry food after moist food counts, and the test takes three months.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these are the permanent tears: if the animal ate moist and dry fodder from an irrigated field, or ate dry fodder and only then moist fodder, it is not a blemish. It becomes a blemish only if the animal eats dry fodder after moist fodder and is still not healed. This period lasts three months.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the ברייתא from the last step. It gives רבי יהודה's rule for when tears count as a permanent blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two kinds of feeding do not count as a real cure attempt: fodder from a בית השלחין, and dry food eaten before moist food. Only the proper order counts, moist first and then dry. If the animal is still not healed after that, the tears are a permanent מום. The whole test runs for three months.

keyTerms.meaning: Permanent (constant) tears, which can be a blemish
An irrigated field that needs watering by hand or by channels

phrases.english: And these are the permanent tears:
If it ate moist and dry fodder
from an irrigated field,
or if it ate dry fodder
and afterward ate the moist fodder,
it is not a blemish
until it eats dry fodder after the moist fodder,
phrases.notes: Only if the animal is still not healed after this order

phrases.english: and this period lasts three months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the ברייתא of רבי יהודה that was brought in step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, tears are a permanent blemish only if the animal stays unhealed after eating moist fodder and then dry fodder, not fodder from an irrigated field. The test lasts three months.

steps.title: The משנה seems to list both field types as no blemish
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that the משנה follows רבי יהודה. The משנה seems to say that rain-watered fodder also proves nothing. But רבי יהודה excluded only irrigated fodder, which implies that rain-watered fodder does count.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned both of them in the משנה: 'it ate moist and dry fodder from a rain-watered field, or moist and dry fodder from an irrigated field' (and both are not a blemish)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 24, which said that the משנה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה mentions two kinds of fields, rain-watered and irrigated, and seems to say that neither feeding proves a blemish. רבי יהודה mentioned only the irrigated field. That implies that for him, rain-watered fodder is a real test. So the משנה and רבי יהודה seem to disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: Rain; here, a field watered only by rain

phrases.english: But we learned both of them:
it ate moist and dry fodder from a rain-watered field,
moist and dry fodder from an irrigated field!
phrases.notes: The משנה seems to treat both as not proving a blemish

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim that the משנה matches רבי יהודה, using the details of the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 24 that the משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה excludes only irrigated fodder, which implies that rain-watered fodder is a valid test. The משנה seems to exclude both kinds of fodder, so the two sources conflict.

steps.title: The משנה is missing words and really agrees with רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is missing words. Correctly read, rain-watered moist-then-dry fodder does prove a blemish. Irrigated fodder does not. Even with rain-watered fodder, dry before moist does not prove anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: Words are missing from the משנה, and this is what it teaches: if it ate moist and dry fodder from a rain-watered field, it is a blemish. If the fodder was from an irrigated field, it is not a blemish. And with rain-watered fodder too, if it ate dry and then moist, it is not a blemish, until it eats dry after moist.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by filling in words it says are missing from the משנה. Read this way, the משנה matches רבי יהודה exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the missing words are added, the משנה no longer puts rain-watered fodder together with irrigated fodder. Rain-watered fodder in the proper order (moist, then dry) is a valid test, so if the animal is not healed, it is a מום. The rain-watered field is mentioned again only to teach that the wrong order (dry, then moist) does not count even there.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what it teaches

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'אָכַל לַח וְיָבֵשׁ' means here 'moist and then dry,' the correct order. That is why rain-watered fodder in that order counts as a real test. 'Dry then moist' is a separate case, and it is not a blemish.
steps.whatToRemember: With the missing words filled in, the משנה follows רבי יהודה. Rain-watered fodder, moist then dry, is a valid test. Irrigated fodder, or dry before moist, is not.

phrases.english: Words are missing,
and this is what it teaches:
if it ate moist and dry fodder from a rain-watered field,
it is a blemish,
phrases.notes: Assuming the animal was not healed

phrases.english: from an irrigated field, it is not a blemish,
and with a rain-watered field too,

phrases.aramaic: אָכַל יָבֵשׁ וְאַחַר כָּךְ אָכַל לַח —
phrases.english: if it ate dry fodder and afterward ate moist fodder,
it is not a blemish,
until it eats dry fodder after the moist fodder.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26 by rereading the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual emendation: words are missing from the משנה (חסורי מיחסרא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה put rain-watered and irrigated fodder together, saying neither proves a blemish.
steps.terutzMaskana: Rain-watered fodder, moist then dry, does prove a blemish. Only irrigated fodder, or dry before moist, does not. This matches רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Do the moist and dry seasons add up to four months?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the three-month length of the test. רב יצחק בר אשיאן said that the moist season is אדר and ניסן and the dry season is אלול and תשרי. That makes four months.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And this period lasts three months.' Is that so? But it was taught, and רב אידי בר אבין said in the name of רב יצחק בר אשיאן: אדר and ניסן are the moist season, and אלול and תשרי are the dry season!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the last words of the ברייתא, the three-month length of the test, and challenges it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יצחק בר אשיאן named the moist season as two months (אדר and ניסן) and the dry season as two months (אלול and תשרי). Two plus two is four months of feeding, not three. So his statement seems to contradict the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: The month of אדר, part of the moist season
The month of אלול, part of the dry season

phrases.english: 'And this period lasts three months.'
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא again in order to challenge it

phrases.english: Is that so?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא — וְהָא רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין
phrases.english: But it was taught, and indeed Rav Idi bar Avin
phrases.notes: The text has a double opening (והתניא / והא); both lead into the same statement

phrases.english: said that Rav Yitzchak bar Ashiyan said:
Adar and Nisan are the moist season,
Elul and Tishrei are the dry season!
phrases.notes: That totals four months, not three

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge on a different detail of the ברייתא: the length of the test.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that the feeding test lasts three months
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב יצחק בר אשיאן gives two moist months and two dry months, which totals four months and contradicts the three months in the ברייתא.

steps.title: Each season is a month and a half
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by rereading רב יצחק בר אשיאן's statement. The moist season is אדר and half of ניסן, and the dry season is אלול and half of תשרי. That totals three months.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: אדר and half of ניסן are the moist season, and אלול and half of תשרי are the dry season.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of רב יצחק בר אשיאן's statement so that it fits the three-month rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the wording changed, each season is a month and a half instead of two months. One and a half plus one and a half equals three months, which matches the ברייתא. The contradiction is gone.
steps.whatToRemember: The feeding test for tears is three months in total: a month and a half of moist fodder (אדר and half of ניסן) and a month and a half of dry fodder (אלול and half of תשרי).

phrases.english: Say instead:
Adar and half of Nisan are the moist season,
Elul and half of Tishrei are the dry season.
phrases.notes: That totals three months

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28 by changing the wording of רב יצחק בר אשיאן's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording (אימא) of the conflicting statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each season was two full months, so the test would be four months.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each season is a month and a half, so the test is three months, as the ברייתא says.

steps.title: Must each fodder be fed in its own season?
steps.stepSummary: An איבעיא: is moist fodder fed in the moist season and dry fodder in the dry season, or are both fed during the moist season?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: Do we feed moist fodder in the moist season and dry fodder in the dry season? Or perhaps we feed both moist and dry fodder during the moist season?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new practical question about the feeding test. It wants to know when each type of fodder must be fed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know the order: moist fodder first, then dry fodder. Now the question is about timing. Option one: wait for the real dry season to feed dry fodder. Option two: during the moist season, feed fresh fodder and then old dry fodder kept from last summer.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked before them (an open question)

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
Moist fodder in the moist season,
and dry fodder in the dry season?
phrases.notes: Each fodder is fed in its natural season.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא: לַח וְיָבֵשׁ בִּזְמַן הַלַּח?
phrases.english: Or perhaps: moist and dry fodder, both in the moist season?
phrases.notes: The dry fodder would be leftover stock from the summer before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting the test at three months, the גמרא asks when within the year each fodder is fed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Must dry fodder be fed in the actual dry season, or may it be fed during the moist season?

steps.title: Proof from the seasons named by רב יצחק בר אשיאן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to answer from רב יצחק בר אשיאן, who named אדר and ניסן as moist and אלול and תשרי as dry.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב אידי בר אבין said in the name of רב יצחק בר אשיאן: אדר and ניסן are moist, and אלול and תשרי are dry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to answer the question. Since the moist and dry fodder are tied to different months, it seems each must be fed in its own season.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יצחק בר אשיאן links each fodder to a season of the year. The proof reads this as the time of feeding. If so, dry fodder must be fed in אלול and תשרי, and the first option of the question is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who defined the moist and dry seasons
The months of the moist season
The months of the dry season

phrases.english: Come and hear,
for Rav Idi bar Avin said
that Rav Yitzchak bar Ashiyan said:
Adar and Nisan are moist,
Elul and Tishrei are dry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question of step 30.
steps.raayaObject: That each fodder must be fed in its own season
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יצחק בר אשיאן's statement assigning moist to אדר and ניסן and dry to אלול and תשרי

steps.title: Maybe the months describe the fodder, not the feeding time
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. Perhaps the months only say when the fodder grows, and the dry produce of אלול and תשרי is fed during אדר and ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps we feed it the produce of אלול and תשרי during אדר and ניסן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof. The statement may only describe which fodder counts as moist or dry, not when it must be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dry months could just be telling us where dry fodder comes from: produce of the late summer. That fodder could still be stored and fed in the spring. So the question stays open.
steps.confusionAlert: רב יצחק בר אשיאן's statement is not being rejected. Only the way the proof read it is rejected: the months may describe the type of fodder, not the time it is fed.

phrases.english: Perhaps the produce of Elul and Tishrei
we feed to it in Adar and Nisan!

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא פֵּירֵי דֶּאֱלוּל וְתִשְׁרִי מַאֲכִילִנַן לֵיהּ בַּאֲדָר וְנִיסָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 31.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. The question is left unresolved.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the months mark the feeding time, but they may only mark when each kind of fodder grows.

steps.title: How much fodder is fed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what amount of fodder is given in the test.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much do we feed it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new detail of the test, the amount of food. This line sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even with the right order, timing, and length of the test, we still need to know how much to feed. A tiny amount might not be a fair test of whether the blemish heals.

phrases.english: And how much do we feed it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the timing question and asks about the amount.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The amount of fodder fed in the test

steps.title: The amount is a dried fig
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, in the name of רבי פנחס בן ערובא, says the amount is a כגרוגרת, the size of a dried fig.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי פנחס בן ערובא: the size of a dried fig.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The animal is fed fodder the size of a dried fig.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גרוגרת is a common measure in הלכה. Here it sets the amount of moist and dry fodder used in the test.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sage quoted by רבי יוחנן
The size of a dried fig

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said
in the name of Rabbi Pinchas ben Arova:
The size of a dried fig.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן עָרוֹבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The animal is fed the size of a dried fig.

steps.title: In ארץ ישראל they asked what the fig size means
steps.stepSummary: רבא reports a question from ארץ ישראל about the fig-sized amount. The first option is that it means a fig size at the first meal. The question continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: They asked in the West (ארץ ישראל): Does it mean a dried fig's amount at the first meal,
steps.whatsHappening: רבא reports a question about how to understand רבי יוחנן's amount. Only the first option appears here; the second option and the rest of the question continue on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The amount is now known, but how it is applied is not. One possibility is that the fig-sized portion is given at the animal's first meal of the day. The other possibility comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: Rava said:
They ask in the West (Eretz Yisrael):
phrases.notes: The text corrects בָּעֵי to בָּעַן, meaning 'they ask'.

phrases.english: a fig-bulk at the first meal,
phrases.notes: The question continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to apply the amount given in step 34.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the fig-sized amount is given at the first meal, or applied some other way (the other option continues on the next amud)
